title: Microsoft Teams: connect a meeting to an existing Planner plan
summary: Hold: the cited PowerShell reference describes the proposed Facilitator blocking command as unblocking an app, so its blocking effect cannot safely be asserted. The roadmap and supplied notice support the planned feature, default availability and rollout window; the rollout wording and Planner licence names also need small corrections.

claims.where: title; front matter: products
claims.claim: Roadmap item 561490 concerns connecting Microsoft Teams meetings to existing Microsoft Planner plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Connect Teams meeting to existing Planner Plans

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Teams meetings currently automatically create corresponding Planner plans for meeting tasks.
claims.quote: Teams meetings automatically create a corresponding Planner plan to capture meeting tasks.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Tasks for a long-running initiative can become scattered across multiple automatically generated plans.
claims.quote: when teams use meetings as their primary collaboration surface for long-running initiatives, tasks from the same project can become scattered across multiple auto-generated plans.

claims.quote: Tasks created during meetings can be added to the selected existing plan.

claims.claim: Premium capabilities require a premium licence such as Planner Plan 1, Project Plan 3 or Project Plan 5.
claims.quote: Users with a Planner premium license such as Planner Plan 1, Project Plan 3, or Project Plan 5, can use the premium capabilities in Planner.
claims.fix: Replace the premium-licence clause with 'premium capabilities need a Planner premium licence such as Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/planner/licensing. The current service description at https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-planner-service-description uses the updated names and says Plan 5 reached end of sale on May 1, 2026, while existing subscriptions can continue.

claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Remove the blocking call from controls[0].api and its rendered table cell. Set the side to null and append to the note: 'Automation for blocking Facilitator is not verified: the cited Update-M365TeamsApp reference labels its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking. Use the documented admin UI.' Do not replace $true with $false: the reference does not establish that correction. This finding concerns contradictory documentation, not verified runtime behaviour.
